newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: FOCUS - Mahathir says stock overspeculation not good.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Mahathir says stock overspeculation not good.

text.p: Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad said on Wednesday that while speculation on the domestic stockmarket creates "thrills", too much speculation can cause people who lost money to commit suicide.

"It's good to have speculation on the stock exchange, but too much speculation becomes bad," he said in a speech at a charity dinner organised by the Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange (KLSE) and Malaysian stockbrokers.

"Sometimes the price goes up without any rhyme or reason. They doubled and trebled and they go up by five, six times especially if they are new issues," he told the gathering of stockbrokers and industry officials.
In a speech laced with humour, he said the stockmarket was designed to help businesses raise capital, but that some had been encouraged by the "thrill" of seeing share prices rise rapidly.
"The stock exchange is a place to raise capital to do business... (but) people soon noticed that when a lot of people buy the same shares they seem to go up.
"And if a lot of people sell, they will come down. These movements give people a lot of thrill," the premier said.
He said he also did not understand why prices of newly-listed stocks should rapidly shoot up when the companies are new to the market.
He said he would not make any presumptions on why these stocks should surge.
"The only thing I know is that it's not a very healthy thing to have new shares to go up that much," Mahathir said.
He said some of the stock price movements are not related to the performance of companies at all.
Due to overspeculation, "a few people unfortunately have to jump off the parapet", he said.
"When you lose money suddenly, you become a little bit giddy and therefore you fall," he added.
He did not say if the government would place new rules to prevent excessive speculation in stocks.
The Malaysian stockmarket has at times been described by analysts as being dominated by excessive punting with trading based on rumours rather than company fundamentals.
Mahathir said he would like stockbrokers to tell him if there was anything he could say to stop share prices from falling further.
"If there is anything I can say which will make the prices go up, just tell me," he said to laughter and loud clapping from the audience.
The key KLSE Composite Index has been battered in recent weeks following the March 28 announcement by the central bank that it was restricting bank loans to the property sector and for buying shares.
The Composite Index closed at 1,109.60 points on Wednesday, down 113.71 points, or 9.30 percent, from its level of 1,223.31 on March 27.
The premier said it was necessary for the central Bank Negara to place the restrictions on properties and share-buying.

"Central bankers are caring people, well-meaning people. They are concerned that too much money is being put in one basket," Mahathir said, hinting at criticisms that Bank Negara's rulings were the main cause of the stockmarket's fall.
-- Kuala Lumpur newsroom (603-201 4813)
